name: Giovanni Gentile
description: Italian philosopher assessed through actual idealism, national education and his arguments for the fascist state, including tensions with independent Church authority.

religion.reason: He explicitly identified as Catholic in 1943; this philosophical identification is distinct from support for clerical political control.

axes.brief: The ethical state transcends liberal party competition and individual political sovereignty.
axes.counterEvidence: Elite educational judgement is not equal popular control; later reconciliation language did not repudiate fascist allegiance.

axes.brief: Freedom is conceived within the state rather than as an independent shield against its political direction.
axes.counterEvidence: Criticism of racial laws and independent intellectual work qualify blanket endorsement of every fascist restriction.

axes.brief: National education and a unified spiritual culture subordinate separate group loyalties.
axes.counterEvidence: Actual idealism is not Nazi biological race theory; criticism of anti-Jewish measures matters.

qualifications.15: The statement specifically includes several distinct ways of life within national identity; it does not ask whether a common national identity should exist.

axes.brief: National-cultural unity favours managed migration and education toward common citizenship.
axes.counterEvidence: No detailed migration programme is documented; anti-Jewish criticism limits ancestry-based conclusions.

qualifications.5: The statement permits permanent refugee settlement regardless of skills or cultural compatibility. The answer concerns this unconditional clause, separately from selected humanitarian admissions.

axes.brief: Interventionist nationalism treats struggle and sacrifice as formative political experiences.
axes.counterEvidence: Philosophical valorisation of struggle is not a recorded answer about AI weapons or every proposed war.

axes.brief: A sovereign ethical national state resists external political constraints.
axes.counterEvidence: Intellectual international exchanges and late dependence on Germany qualify a literal claim of isolated self-sufficiency.

axes.brief: State primacy is compatible with subordinate private production and education.
axes.counterEvidence: Philosophical statism does not automatically require nationalisation of every business or hospital.

axes.brief: National interests qualify private international exchange and foreign control of strategic assets.
axes.counterEvidence: The philosophical dossier does not specify a tariff schedule; these are weak economic-mechanism estimates.

axes.brief: The state may coordinate production toward national purposes while allowing private initiative.
axes.counterEvidence: Actualism is a theory of political spirit, not a fully specified economic plan or currency programme.

axes.brief: Hierarchical educational selection coexists with collective duties and bounded social support.
axes.counterEvidence: Educational merit and spiritual equality do not establish a tax-and-transfer equalisation programme.

axes.brief: Religion has an educational-cultural role, but independent Church sovereignty conflicts with the ethical state.
axes.counterEvidence: Primary-school religious instruction and personal Catholic identification constrain a wholly secular reading.

axes.brief: Elite national education and conventional family assumptions favour established moral norms.
axes.counterEvidence: The fascist project sought a new political character; political revolution is independent of gender equality.

axes.brief: National intellectual renewal favours development with ethical and educational guidance.
axes.counterEvidence: His humanities-centred school hierarchy complicates unrestricted technocratic enthusiasm.

axes.brief: National state unity and centrally structured education limit autonomous regional institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Local administration remains compatible with hierarchy; it is not independent constitutional sovereignty.

axes.brief: Actual idealism gives formative thought, culture and education priority over biological reductionism.
axes.counterEvidence: Philosophical mind primacy is not a measured claim that inherited dispositions never contribute to individual traits.
